meta.title: Sahyadri Krida Mandal
meta.foundedNote: The mandal states 1976 for its organisation; Mid-day (2009) dates the first festival to 1977, while Rediff (2016) says the organisation formed in 1975. These retrospective dates are not silently reconciled. Inaugural minutes or a period souvenir remain needed.
meta.intro: Sahyadri Krida Mandal organises a public Ganesh festival at Tilak Nagar in Chembur. Its history joins a neighbourhood sports organisation to elaborate temporary scenery and the work of sculptors and stage designers. The mandal dates its establishment to 1976; an earlier newspaper account places the festival's beginning in 1977. Its online retrospective offers year-labelled photographs, giving this collection a documented starting point for comparing Ganesh forms and physical settings without treating those selected images as a complete annual archive.

sections.title: A sports club and a public festival

paragraphs.text: The mandal dates its organisation to 1976, while Mid-day's 2009 account puts the first public festival in 1977. Rediff's 2016 retrospective instead says the organisation formed in 1975. The sources do not explain these differences, so the exact founding chronology remains open. The locality and venue history can be documented without inventing a single settled anniversary.

Mid-day reports that the festival moved to a nearby municipal ground in 1980. Its short history names art directors Sudhakar Manjarekar and Roderick D'Souza among those who created decorative sets over the years. This establishes a history of designed festival space, while leaving the precise years and authorship of individual sets open to further documentation.

Ganesh Chitra Mandir's family history associates sculptor Vishnu Bhagwan “Babi” Bandekar with Sahyadri's twelve-foot idol and a 1992 Orient-Samana first prize. This is the workshop's own retrospective account, not an independently located award record. Contemporary reporting by Bella Jaisinghani in 2023 separately names Pratibha Bandekar of Sahyadri Krida Mandal among a younger generation of established sculptors.

The official gallery provides Marathi and English year labels. Its 2005 photographs show a cloud-and-star setting, including a smaller foreground Ganesh and a larger Ganesh deeper inside the set. The 2024 selection includes both a seated Ganesh portrait and an exterior dominated by Hanuman imagery. These are distinct photographs of the idol and its surrounding temporary scenery, not evidence that every figure in the set is the festival Ganesh.

The expanded visual sequence shows both continuity and changes in presentation: a glittering cross-legged form within a transparent dome in the 2007-labelled image, a turbaned seated form in 2013 and 2016, horse-and-elephant columns in 2018, and peacock motifs in 2023. These are observations of physical scenes. Their years remain retrospective gallery attributions, not independently verified capture dates. Two catalogue captions are mismatched: the 2010 image labelled Ganesh is an exterior, and the 2025 image labelled a silver Mahadev form is a palace facade.

The 2016 Panda Village has contemporary corroboration beyond the retrospective gallery. The Indian Express reported the film-inspired set during preparation; Rediff subsequently described the operating installation and named Prasoonjit Chanda as its scenic designer. This is a year-specific set-design credit, not an attribution of the Ganesh sculpture or every later commission.

The mandal describes medical help, food distribution, educational assistance and environmental work as part of its wider purpose. Its account also emphasises residents, younger volunteers and senior guides. This is a useful institutional statement of community aims; particular projects, dates and outcomes still need separate records before being added as verified milestones.

researchNotes.coverage: Expanded research, 16 November 2026: seven additional year-labelled physical photographs, visual correction of mismatched captions, contemporary 2016 scenic-design reporting and a newly exposed founding-date disagreement. Nine located years; not a complete annual chronology.
gaps: No 1970s primary records or first-generation photographs.
Official images lack named photographers and open licensing.
Retrospective gallery contains mismatched captions; selected years require original-file corroboration.
Formation is reported as 1975 and 1976; first-festival account says 1977.
